## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

### What is an earnings surprise? [...] Most publicly traded companies report earnings four times a year, once per fiscal quarter. Earnings season typically begins a few weeks after each quarter ends, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. Not all companies report on the same date, so the Earnings Calendar helps you track which companies are reporting on any given day.

## How to use the Earnings Calendar?

TradingView’s Earnings Calendar shows the latest and upcoming earnings reports released by companies. As an important indicator of a company’s financial state, earnings per share are one of the most followed metrics among traders, so the calendar above can serve as a powerful tool for analysis.

For firms that only need earnings announcement information, the earnings calendar features upcoming earnings calendar dates - confirmed or forecasted, with the expected timing of announcements. This includes preliminary earnings announcements.

Need to know when earnings dates change and why?

#### DateBreaks - Earnings Date Revisions [...] With the new Interim Calendar, institutional investors and traders can access critical dates and information when public companies report key sales, production and financial information between their quarterly or semi-annual earnings announcements.
